items.title: The billion-dollar game Australia is taking time off to play
paras: Grand Theft Auto 6 is expected to be one of the most expensive games ever created. ( Supplied: Rockstar Games )
When the clock edges past midnight tomorrow morning, power usage will surge as gamers across the globe boot up the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 for the first time.
The Grand Theft Auto (GTA) series has been a touchstone of gaming since developer Rockstar Games launched the series in 1997.
Plagued by delays and leaks, the latest instalment is predicted to break financial records, which it will need to do considering the staggering investment by Rockstar.
Set in a fictional, Florida-inspired state, GTA 6 follows leads Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and has been a source of considerable hype in the lead-up to its release .
A recurring location in the GTA series, Vice City is a virtual parallel to Miami. ( Supplied: Rockstar Games )
Game reviewer Ben Schuster said this was the most expensive video game ever made, telling the ABC its budget was likely between $US1.5 billion and $US2b.
He said the spend was expected to translate into something "on a completely different scale".
Ben Schuster expects the world of GTA 6 will be the most detailed and complex to date. ( Supplied: Rockstar Games )
"The detail in Grand Theft Auto 6 is something that we've probably never seen to date and is quite possibly the biggest entertainment undertaking in history," Mr Schuster said.
For fans of the series, waiting until the weekend simply won't do, so they have booked in annual leave.
Danny, who played more than 3,000 hours on GTA 5, has taken four days off to explore the game.
Danny and fellow GTA fan Hayden are looking forward to the game's release. ( Supplied )
He's aiming to finish it before heading back to work, over fears of having anything spoiled.
"I’m expecting just a really well written story ... a very well-crafted world, something I can immerse and get lost into."
He's most excited to walk down the streets of Vice City, a parallel to Miami, and talk to pedestrians.
Grand Theft Auto is a sandbox game, meaning players are unleashed on the open world and free to do as they please. ( Supplied: Rockstar Games )

In response to growing concerns over gamers "chucking a sickie", the Fair Work Ombudsman posted a pointed reminder online: that when taking sick leave you may be asked for evidence of illness or injury.
In 2013, previous iteration GTA 5 became one of the best-selling games of all time with more than 255 million copies sold, forcing its way into the pop culture Zeitgeist.
"I don't think you have to be an elite gamer to enjoy Grand Theft Auto," Mr Schuster said.
"It is a series that defines not only a generation of consoles, but also a generation of people who play them.
"These games have unsurpassed detail and set the bar for every game that follows it."
Lachlan May is part of the GTA generation, having played earlier games when he was young and clocking countless hours in GTA 5.
Lachlan May says the release of GTA 6 felt like a day that was never going to come. ( Supplied )
During the isolating COVID years, Mr May socialised with friends through GTA 5.
He even got a tattoo to commemorate his love for the series ahead of tomorrow.
Lachlan May got a GTA 5 tattoo ahead of the sixth game's launch. ( Supplied )
Some Australian gamers are shaping their weeks, holidays and social lives around the release.
Harrison Engstrom, from Melbourne, is hosting half a dozen friends for a breakfast barbecue as they enjoy the launch together.
"Even if everything goes awful, at least we'll make the best of the situation," Mr Engstrom said.
Aaiden Court is staying up until midnight to play the game immediately, but the release coincides with a camping trip.
Zaina Molna believes GTA 6 will meet expectations due to the quality of Rockstar's previous release, Red Dead Redemption 2. ( Supplied )
Melbourne-based logistics coordinator Zaina Molnar is flying home from her sister's wedding in Fiji at 7pm tomorrow, but she has a plan.
"I'm hoping customs won't be that busy so I can take an Uber from the airport to the shopping centre," Ms Molnar said.
She plans to pick up a copy of the game, rush home to start the download, take a four-hour nap, then wake up for an all-night gaming sesh.
"My mind won’t be where it should be, working, it will be on GTA," she said.
According to digital analytics company Sensor Tower, almost 15 million copies of GTA 6 have been pre-ordered, and Forbes has reported the game is expected to make almost $4.5b in its opening week.
"Eighty-two per cent of Australians play video games," Mr Schuster said.
"When you consider that, a lot of people in Australia, a lot of workers will be playing Grand Theft Auto 6."
Due to the size of the game, players have been able to download it ahead of time.
Downloads opened on November 10, and the National Broadband Network confirmed it had experienced an uptick in network use by 2 to 3.5 terabits per second.
The star system returns in GTA 6, where an escalating number of police will chase players depending on the severity of the crime committed. ( Supplied: Rockstar Games )
"This game download is about 40 per cent of what the average home downloads in a month," an NBN spokesperson said.

items.title: ‘I made serious mistakes’: Jensen Huang opens up as he pushes for return to Nvidia
paras: Advertisement Business Companies Executive shake-up ‘I made serious mistakes’: Jensen Huang opens up as he pushes for return to Nvidia Ian King November 18, 2026 — 5:31am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A Former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang has expressed willingness to return to the helm after his dramatic ouster last week, though the board isn’t currently considering such an idea.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a statement. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang wants to return to the company. Bloomberg via Getty Images The company cut ties with Huang after the revelation that he’d had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is now under investigation for potentially spying on behalf of China.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang said in the statement. “I created problems for the board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.”

As of Tuesday (US time), the Nvidia board is not considering bringing Huang back, according to a person familiar with the board’s thinking. The directors have begun a hunt for a new leader while chief financial officer Colette Kress serves as interim CEO. Nvidia tapped executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead the process, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Meanwhile, Huang has agreed to brief Congress next month on his affair with the suspected Chinese spy. Huang will appear before a joint meeting of the House Intelligence, Foreign Affairs and China Select committees on December 1, according to a statement from the panels’ chairmen.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries told reporters at the US Capitol that Huang shouldn’t return as CEO. Asked whether the board should rehire Huang, Jeffries responded, “No.” He added that while the decision is ultimately up to the company’s board, Huang’s actions were “unacceptable.”

Since his exit, President Donald Trump and influential executives have discussed the idea of Huang returning as CEO . In a social media post, investment firms Altimeter Capital Management and Atreides Management cited “the extraordinary success of Jensen Huang’s leadership over a long period of time” and the uncertainty created by his departure in urging the board to take a “slow, measured, and deliberate” approach to Nvidia’s future leadership.

That should include “the potential return of Jensen Huang,” Altimeter’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides’ Gavin Baker wrote in a letter to Nvidia’s board posted on X. SpaceX and Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk has also expressed support for a comeback.
Trump said he “would not mind” the idea of Huang returning. “A lot of people are asking Jensen — they think Jensen should go back,” Trump told reporters Monday. “That certainly isn’t a bad idea.”

Donald Trump and Elon Musk have advocated for Huang’s return to the top job at Nvidia. AP Lisa Su, head of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices, was also asked about the scandal that has engulfed her biggest competitor. “Jensen has been an incredible leader,” she said at a conference in Austin on Tuesday. “But we have to separate from the noise.”

Huang transformed the company from a maker of PC gaming components into the main beneficiary of the AI revolution. Along the way, Nvidia’s sales surged to a level never seen in the chip industry — and the company was the first to cross a valuation of $US5 trillion ($7.4 trillion).

The Nvidia board officially parted ways with the 63-year-old cofounder on November 12 after the controversy surrounding his affairs grew into a crisis spanning Silicon Valley, Washington and Beijing. US lawmakers have sought answers from the executive about the alleged espionage plot, while Beijing has denied that it attempted to spy on Huang.

Nvidia named chief financial officer Colette Kress as an interim leader while it searches for Huang’s permanent replacement. It also elevated board member Harvey Jones to the role of chairman, a job Nvidia hadn’t had before.

items.title: US tech billionaire flags interest in Hurricanes, Hobart stadium
paras: Sanjay Govil has expressed interest in buying into the Hobart Hurricanes Big Bash League team. ( Getty Images: Steve Bell )
Tech billionaire Sanjay Govil has expressed interest in buying into the Hobart Hurricanes and the Hobart stadium precinct.
The government's appetite for such a deal is unclear, and any public-private partnership agreement for the stadium would signal a change in policy.
An updated cost for the Hobart stadium project is expected in the next few weeks.
Cricket looms as a wildcard in the Tasmanian government's hunt for more funds to build the new Macquarie Point stadium.
And at least one American billionaire has expressed an interest in investing in the stadium precinct , as part of a potential power play involving the Hobart Hurricanes cricket team.
Tech billionaire Sanjay Govil wants to buy at least a 50 per cent share in the Hobart Hurricanes, following Cricket Australia's decision to green-light the privatisation of the Big Bash League.

As part of a broader cricket and infrastructure play, Mr Govil is interested in a slice of the Macquarie Point stadium and precinct, envisioning a place where American college football-style parties may be held before future Hurricanes games.
"I think it's going to be very, very exciting. And to be part of that? Imagine," he told the ABC.
Sanjay Govil has expressed interest in the Hobart Hurricanes and Macquarie Point stadium project. ( Supplied: Eagle Team )
Mr Govil, who founded Infinite Computer Solutions and digital healthcare company Zyter, is worth upwards of US$2 billion.

He owns the Welsh Fire, which plays in the UK Hundred competition, the Ricky Ponting-coached Washington Freedom in America's Major League Cricket competition, and is funding the construction of a 10,000-capacity cricket stadium for the Freedom in Frederick, Maryland.
He wants a stake in the Big Bash League and has targeted the Hurricanes — and its prospective new stadium.

"We would come in, and part A is the operations team, taking ownership of the Hobart Hurricanes team. The Hurricanes would then, in turn, lease the ground and facility from entity B, which would have different shareholders including us," he said.
Sanjay Govil says it would be "exciting" to have a stake in the Macquarie Point stadium. ( Supplied: Cox Architecture )

The Auburn college football fan, who also owns a stake in entertainment and events company Mari, envisages a college football-style atmosphere and fan experiences before and after Hurricanes games at Macquarie Point.
"That infrastructure would not just include the stadium, but a tailgating area, shops, restaurants, a whole experience centre," he said.
"It's all about experience. That's the expertise I want to bring to the Hobart Hurricanes.
The prospect of cricket-induced private investment was floated with Premier Jeremy Rockliff at a September 8 meeting between him and Cricket Tasmania bosses.
The government's appetite for such a deal is unclear, and any public-private partnership agreement would signal a backflip.

It had previously explored a public-private partnership for the stadium, commissioning reports by Perth consultants Paxon Group and Melbourne-based Infrastructure Advisory Group last year — but ultimately decided against the model, deeming it too high a risk to the state .
But with a stadium budget crunch on the horizon, a cricket-flavoured public-private partnership might become enticing to a government desperately needing outside funds to help fund the build.

The stadium looks set to exceed its project budget of $1.13 billion, with state funding constrained to $875 million, as part of a government agreement with upper house MLC Bec Thomas in exchange for her support for the project in Tasmania's parliament last year.
BESIX Watpac won the tender to construct the Macquarie Point stadium. ( ABC News: Kate Nickels )

The remainder of the project budget is made up of a $240 million contribution from the federal government and $15 million from the AFL, with any further required funds to be sought from those partners, cricket, or the private sector .
The government may also be wary about entering such a partnership, after a parliamentary inquiry panned its most recent dalliance with a sporting billionaire .

That deal, between the government and National Basketball League owner Larry Kestelman, involved a taxpayer-funded revamp of the former Derwent Entertainment Centre, and the government entering into an exclusive negotiation process with Mr Kestelman over the sale of 15 hectares of land at neighbouring Wilkinsons Point.
In exchange, Mr Kestelman granted Tasmania an NBL licence — the JackJumpers — and promised to undertake an up to $500 million development on the land.
The state government's deal with Larry Kestelman was panned by a parliamentary committee. ( ABC News: Luke Bowden )
More than five years on, no development has commenced as the two parties wrangle over costs, and the inquiry continues.

A sell-off of commercially zoned land at Macquarie Point is planned to follow substantial commencement of the stadium build, with the Macquarie Point Development Corporation hoping to raise at least $85 million from that process.
Under current plans, Stadiums Tasmania will own and operate the venue once it is built, and it is highly likely the sale of land parcels at Macquarie Point will be subject to an open-market process.
It is understood there is no shortage of interest in the Hurricanes and Macquarie Point, with Cricket Tasmania fielding calls from India, the UK and the US about a potential deal.
In June, Cricket Tasmania boss Dominic Baker told the ABC he wanted to partner with a team owner who was "willing to invest in Tasmania" and cited the stadium project as a major attractor.

Mr Govil is particularly keen to add the Hurricanes to his stable of teams but is aware that the prospect of owning a piece of Macquarie Point, as well as the Hurricanes, remains firmly in the preliminary stages.
"Step two then comes in, and that's a new bridge you have to cross, and we'll cross it accordingly."
Kristie Johnston says there are many questions. ( ABC News: Owain Stia James )
Independent MP Kristie Johnston, who has long advocated against the stadium, questioned any pivot towards a public-private partnership.

Negotiations between the Macquarie Point Development Corporation and Watpac Construction officially concluded last week, with the builder providing the MPDC an official fixed-price, lump-sum cost number to build the stadium.
That number is so far unknown — but will differ from the overall project budget, which is expected to exceed the allotted $1.13 billion.

items.title: Everything you need to know before tonight's ARIAs
paras: Tame Impala, Genesis Owusu, and Ecca Vandal lead the nominees at tonight's ARIA Awards. ( Supplied )
On Monday afternoon, the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) sent an email with a clear message.
The message detailed a new campaign urging the Australian government to stay firm on not allowing AI companies to use Australian creative work to train their models without permission.
"Australia's creative and media sector adds $70.3 billion to the economy and supports almost 600,000 workers," ARIA's letter read.
"Decisions now in front of the government could undo the copyright protections our industry runs on."
At Sydney's Hordern Pavilion tonight, they host the ARIA Awards for the 40th time. These are Australia's pre-eminent music awards, with a long history and a slot on prime-time TV.
If ARIA wants to draw attention to their key issue, this is the week to do it.
While the debate around AI may loom large over the ceremony, it's far from the only story of the night.
This year's nominations are dominated by Canberran genre-smasher Genesis Owusu, and Kevin Parker's Tame Impala, with eight apiece.
Victorian noise monger Ecca Vandal received her first ARIA nominations this year, picking up six of them for her second album Looking for People to Unfollow.
Ninajirachi, Baker Boy, Miss Kaninna, G Flip and Boy Soda all follow closely with five nominations each.
The Album of the Year race is between Owusu, Vandal, Tame Impala, indie rockers DMA's and soul sensation Boy Soda.
Both Owusu and Tame Impala have won the award multiple times and go in as the artists to beat.

Should Tame Impala win for their fifth album Deadbeat, Kevin Parker will become the outright highest-winning artist in the category's history after previously winning in 2013, 2015 and 2020. He currently shares the honour with Aussie rock royalty Powderfinger .
Owusu has a positive history with the awards, winning four trophies in 2021 and three in 2023. But even his seven gongs pale compared to the 13 Parker has taken home.

Both Owusu and Ecca Vandal have been in the winner's circle this month: the former winning Album of the Year at last week's J Awards , the latter picking up the $30,000 Australian Music Prize the week prior.

While it's possible Parker sweeps the field again tonight and picks up multiple trophies, he faces stiff competition across several categories, including Best Pop Release, where he's up against stars like Troye Sivan and Kylie Minogue.
Parker has already been confirmed as the winner of the Global Impact Award, recognising his international success and cultural influence over the past 12 months, so he won't go home empty-handed.
British singer Sienna Spiro will perform at the 2026 ARIA Awards. ( Supplied: ARIA )
Nominees Genesis Owusu, Ecca Vandal, DMA's and Boy Soda will all perform at the awards this year. As will 3%, Scribe and Fred Leone, and recent ARIA Hall of Fame inductees Spiderbait .
ARIA has also locked in 21-year-old British jazz-pop star Sienna Spiro, who will offer a taste of what's to come on her largely sold-out Australian tour next January.
The show is hosted by Melanie Bracewell and Tim McDonald, and presenting guests will include Spice Girl Melanie C and local favourites like Jimmy Barnes, The Veronicas, Baker Boy and G Flip.
The music industry's biggest concern and biggest celebration will almost certainly coalesce.
Musicians don't love staying quiet, and while ARIA may not always love all the statements that speeches cover, this year will be different.
The question is: who will make the biggest stand, and what will it look like?
It's rare to have such a high percentage of people in the room singing from the same sheet, as they do in opposition to AI.
And with ARIA themselves making noise about big tech's use of Australian creators' work to train their products, there'll be little fear of repercussions. The gloves could come off.
You can see all the stars on the red carpet on ARIA's social media accounts from 1pm AEDT.
The ARIA Awards themselves are broadcast live on Paramount+ from 5pm AEDT with a delayed broadcast slated for Channel Ten at 8:45pm.
We'll have our ARIAs live blog firing from 4:20pm AEDT and our list of all the ARIA award winners updated live as the awards are handed out.

items.title: Quiz: See how Robert Pattinson compares with previous Bonds
paras: From Connery to Craig, and now Pattinson, rank the Bonds and their films.
We have a new Bond, and he's Batman. And a Hufflepuff. And a vampire, who is also recently returned from ancient Greece.

Robert Pattinson, 40, was unveiled as the next 007 yesterday . While there's not yet a release date for his first outing in the role, he'll likely be 41 or 42 by the time the next Bond film premieres. So how does that compare with previous Bonds?
Your mission in this More Or Less quiz is to rank the Bond actors , Bond actresses , Bond films and Bond songs in their correct order.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "High probability of meeting between PM Modi, President Xi": Former Indian envoy on patrolling agreement between India-C
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Gautam Bambawale , former India n Ambassador to China , Bhutan, and Pakistan said that the recent agreement on border patrolling between India and China along the Line of Actual Control ( LAC ) has opened up possibilities for a bilateral meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping in Kazan along the sidelines of the BRICS Summit and asserted that the probability of a meeting between the two leaders is "very high." He also noted that although India and China reached an agreement on patrolling arrangements ahead of the BRICS Summit in Kazan , Russia , this breakthrough is the result of discussions and negotiations between India and China , with no involvement from Russia . While speaking with ANI, Bambawale said, "On this question of the recent agreement on patrolling along the LAC , especially in eastern Ladakh, I do not think the Russia ns must have had a hand in it. It would have been discussions between India and China and negotiations between India and China that led to this agreement." He added, "Now that the problems on the border along the LAC have been sorted out, I think there is a very high probability that our Prime Minister Modi and the President of China , Xi Jinping , could have a bilateral meeting in Kazan . I think it would be a meeting to break the ice. I don't expect some great warmth suddenly. It will take time to rebuild the relationship from the setback that it had in the Summer of 2020. This situation has gone on for 4.5 years. So it will take some time to repair the relationship but I think this agreement will be a start and if there's a meeting between the two leaders at the summit level in Kazan on the sidelines of BRICS, then that will be another step towards restoring the relationship to what it was earlier." Bambawale further said that the agreement on patrolling arrangements implies that China is willing to restore the relationship between the two nations to its pre-2020 state, paving the way for progress in other sectors such as trade, commerce, and investment.

He said, "The agreement has come just before the BRICS summit takes place in the next few days in Kazan in Russia . I think what this implies is that the Chinese side is wanting to restore the relationship between India and China to what it was earlier. It wants the other aspects of the relationship like trade, commerce and investment to move ahead. It will of course take some time to restore the trust between the two countries. But at least I think a beginning can be made and perhaps there might be a meeting at the topmost level between PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping at Kazan ." The former India n Ambassador further noted that the agreement between India and China is expected to significantly boost the BRICS grouping, despite not necessarily indicating a closer relationship between India and Russia or China . "I won't say India is moving closer to Russia and China but I think the BRICS grouping will be immeasurably strengthened because of this understanding between India and China because of the cooling of tensions on the border between India and China and as India has always said that a peaceful border means that the rest of the relatrionship can also move ahead. So I believe that a better relationship between India and China will be better for the BRICS grouping," Bambawale told ANI. Bambawale further said, "If this implies that the status quo ante has been restored as it existed before the Chinese undertook the military action in eastern Ladakh in summer of 2020... then I think this is a very welcome development. The government of India should be congratulated on taking a firm position on this matter and that India 's stand has been vindicated after 4.5 years of face-to-face situation between India n and Chinese troops. If it means that the status quo ante has been restored, then we definitely welcome this agreement. It is a good agreement and we can move forward on the basis of this agreement." Notably, a day before, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, who addressed a special media briefing ahead of PM Modi 's visit to Russia for the BRICS Summit , said India and China have reached an agreement on the patrolling arrangements along LAC . The agreement was reached ahead of the BRICS Summit which will be attended by PM Modi and Chinese President Xi. "On several areas along the Line of Actual Control , we held discussions with Chinese interlocutors, both on diplomatic as well as the military levels through meeting with military commanders at various levels. These discussions had in the past resulted in the resolution of standoffs at various locations. There are some locations and areas where stand-offs had not been resolved," said Misri. "Now, as a result of the discussions taking place over the last several weeks an agreement has been arrived at on patrolling arrangements along the LAC in the India - China border areas. This is leading to disengagement and eventually a resolution of the issues that had arisen in these areas in 2020," he added. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: We now know how radiation destroys electronics devices
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print Electronic circuit board Mentor57/Shutterstock Researchers are gaining a new understanding of exactly how radiation destroys electronics devices. The work is a step towards building more resilient electronics for use in nuclear fusion experiments or in space.

Cristyan Quiñones at North Carolina State University stayed up for nearly three days so he could watch a beam of heavy ions destroy an array of electronics devices. It was a high stakes experiment: few labs around the world operate heavy ion beams and securing access to run experiments is difficult. But it is only with experiments like this that researchers can systematically study dangers that electronics devices would encounter onboard a satellite or near a nuclear reactor.

In those challenging high-radiation environments, electronics devices can dramatically and rapidly fail during what is called a “single-event burnout” (SEB). Thanks to their experiments, Quiñones and his colleagues have now zeroed in on exactly how SEB happens.

The team focused on electronics components called diodes that they built from aluminium nitride, a semiconductor made from aluminium and nitrogen. Similar diodes are used to help power electronics devices, and aluminium nitride has been put forward as a promising foundation for the next generation of such power components.

Researchers have also theorised that aluminium nitride is resilient to radiation exposure, which would make it a good choice for use in high-radiation environments such as space . But this idea has not been thoroughly investigated in experiments, says team-member Ramón Collazo , also at North Carolina State University.

In the new experiment, which also involved researchers from NASA, energetic ions of silver, gold or the rare-earth metal praseodymium hit and entered each aluminium nitride diode and the researchers tracked how much electric voltage the diode could then sustain before SEB destroyed it.

Through data analysis and computer simulations, they found that each ion caused a disturbance within the diode, which, combined with the voltage, created a localised electric field. At some threshold voltage, that field became strong enough for nearby electrons to flock towards it, and this avalanche of electrons onto the small area led to a miniature explosion.

Microscope images from the experiment clearly showed tiny, melted craters in the aluminium nitride diode where SEB happened in this way. Additionally, comparing aluminium nitride to similar semiconductors, the team determined that it could withstand higher electrical fields before exploding, but relatively low voltages. Such a systematic and careful comparison had not been done before, but will inform how the material is used going forward.
A storm as powerful as the Carrington event of 1859 might cause some issues, says a reader, but modern planes have a lot of safeguards built in. You should be more worried about “superflares”

Understanding SEB is important because it is among the biggest challenges for making electronics reliable in space, says Ronald Schrimpf at Vanderbilt University in Tennessee, who wasn’t involved with the experiment. He says that power systems are often the most vulnerable part of an overall spacecraft, with phenomena like SEB occurring even when there are physical shields to protect electronics , so studying proposed power device materials that are potentially more resilient, like aluminium nitride, is timely. “If your power supply goes down, nothing works, right?” says Schrimpf.

While radiation-resilient electronics are important in nuclear engineering and a variety of other settings, including the technology used in radiation therapy for cancers, they recently gained more attention because of proposals to put data centres into space. But Schrimpf says that making electronics ready for space is a complex scientific problem that also encounters logistical challenges because the facilities for testing electronics materials, such as the ion beam in the new experiment, are scarce. For Collazo, uncovering physical processes such as the electron avalanche in aluminium nitride is key for innovation in this area.

“Cristyan is telling us the physics of what is happening. You can now design the device around it because you know what is actually causing the problem,” he says. The team are now working on developing designs principles based on what they have learned about SEB so far, says Collazo.

items.title: Humanity braces for an alien invasion in 3 Body Problem S2 teaser
paras: “We’ve been watching.” Humanity braces for an alien invasion in 3 Body Problem S2 teaser “Wake up! They haven’t come 24 trillion miles to negotiate. They are coming to exterminate us.”

9 ... ... ... Credit: Netflix Credit: Netflix Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav You might be excused for forgetting about the existence of 3 Body Problem , Netflix’s heady sci-fi series adapted from the award-winning novel The Three-Body Problem by Liu Cixin, the first book in his Remembrance of Earth’s Past trilogy. After all, it debuted in March 2024. But it was an exceptionally well-done, thematically rich series, and we’re finally getting the second of a planned three seasons in January. Netflix just dropped the first teaser.

Created by David Benioff, D.B. Weiss ( Game of Thrones ), and Alexander Woo ( True Blood ), the first season followed two primary timelines. In the earlier one, a young Chinese astrophysicist, Ye Wenjie (Rosalind Chao), witnessed her father being beaten to death by Red Guards during the Cultural Revolution. Ye figured out a means of sending an interstellar message to possible extraterrestrial civilizations, receiving a response from a planet called Trisolaris.

The planet had three suns, which wreaked havoc on Trisolaris via unpredictable “chaotic periods”—hence the novel’s title, which refers to a classic problem in celestial mechanics. Despite being warned that the aliens intended to invade and conquer Earth, Ye responded to the message and invited them to do so, bitter and disillusioned by the state of the world. She eventually became an established professor (Zine Tseng played the older version).

In the present day, the consequences of Ye’s fateful decision began to play out, beginning with a series of mysterious suicides by scientists, many of whom had possessed a highly advanced VR gaming headset. Among the dead: a particle physicist named Vera Ye (daughter of Ye Wenjie). Five of her former students (known as the Oxford Five) joined forces to figure out what was going on, eventually finding themselves caught in a global fight to save Earth from the invading Trisolarians (or San-Ti). Another human cult faction was just as intent on enabling the San-Ti invasion, believing they would be spared as a reward, while Ye Wenjie still believed the entire human race deserved to be annihilated.

The second season will adapt the second novel in the series, The Dark Forest , with the third book, Death’s End , serving as source material for the third season. Per the official S2 synopsis: “As the alien invasion nears, humanity prepares to meet them—on Earth and beyond. While a space fleet embarks on a mission that spans centuries, a secret locked inside of one man’s mind might be humanity’s only hope for survival.”

(L to R) Jovan Adep, Josh Brener, Benedict Wong, Liam Cunningham, and Jess Hong return for S2. Netflix Sophon (Sea Shimooka) is the intelligence platform the aliens use to communicate with humans. Netflix Sophon (Sea Shimooka) is the intelligence platform the aliens use to communicate with humans. Netflix An ominous message from the San-Ti. Netflix An ominous message from the San-Ti. Netflix Sophon (Sea Shimooka) is the intelligence platform the aliens use to communicate with humans. Netflix An ominous message from the San-Ti. Netflix We lost two members of the Oxford Five in S1: Jack Rooney (John Bradley), killed by cult member Tatiana (Marlo Kelly); and physics teacher Will Downing (Alex Sharp), who was dying of cancer and chose to euthanize himself and donate his cryogenically frozen brain to a bold effort to stave off the invasion. (While the probe carrying Will’s brain veered off-course in the season finale, the original plan was for the San-Ti to use the brain to reconstruct his body, so some version of Will could show up again.)

Kelly’s Tatiana is returning for S2, along with surviving Oxford Five members Jin Cheng (Jess Hong), Saul Durand (Jovan Adepo), and Auggie Salazar (Eiza Gonzalez), whose pioneering nanofibers were memorably used in S1 to slice through a ship in the Panama Canal, killing all the pro-alien cult members on board in gruesome fashion. Also returning are Liam Cunningham as Thomas Wade; Benedict Wong as MI6 agent Clarence “Da” Shi; Sea Shimooka as Sophon, an avatar in the show’s mysterious VR game; and Saamer Usmani as Jin’s Royal Navy officer boyfriend Prithviraj Varma.
New cast members include Claudia Doumit as Captain Van Rijn and Ellie de Lange as Ayla. In addition, Alfie Allen, David Yip, and Jordan Sunshine will appear in as-yet-undisclosed guest roles.
The second season of 3 Body Problem drops on Netflix on January 14, 2027.

items.title: Sam Querrey suggests if he believes Rafael Nadal would trade a Grand Slam for an ATP Finals title
paras: Rafael Nadal won 22 Grand Slams but never lifted the ATP Finals trophy. The Spaniard was twice a runner-up at the ATP Finals, losing to Roger Federer in 2010 and to Novak Djokovic in 2013.

For all his success elsewhere on tour, Nadal couldn’t quite figure out how to win the year-end championships. But would Nadal trade one of his Grand Slam titles, in particular one of his 14 Roland Garros titles, for an ATP Finals crown?

Former American ATP stars Sam Querrey and Steve Johnson have shared their thoughts. “I know [ATP Finals] they are a massive deal. I don’t think guys think of it like, ‘Gosh’. I don’t think Rafa [Nadal] is like, ‘Man, I wish I would have had that one.’ The general tennis community, I’m still convinced, cares about Slams only,” said Querrey on the ‘ Nothing Major ‘ podcast.

items.title: Mirra Andreeva has a new challenge to overcome in 2027 following her WTA Finals win
paras: The Russian superstar came into 2026 as a two-time WTA 1000 champion. However, she had yet to win the sport’s greatest honours. Andreeva added her name to the exclusive club of Grand Slam winners when she defeated Maja Chwalinska in the 2026 Roland Garros final.

Five months later, Andreeva won her first WTA Finals title . Andreeva can now bask in the glory of her 2026 campaign and prepare appropriately for next season. The teenager will need to make sure she is well prepared, as a new challenge awaits her.

Will Mirra Andreeva hit double figures for majors? The 19-year-old is a Grand Slam champion, a WTA Finals champion and the new world number two. Andreeva may even claim the world number one ranking at the start of 2027. After all, she trails Elena Rybakina by only 293 points in the standings.
items.impact: The Kazakhstani star won two Grand Slam titles – beating Aryna Sabalenka in the Australian Open and US Open finals – and achieved the world number one ranking for the first time in her career.

items.title: Meet the only player to defeat Daniil Medvedev in an ATP match after losing the first set this year
paras: Daniil Medvedev began his ATP Finals campaign with victory on Monday evening. The former world number one took a big step towards securing a semi-final berth in Turin after defeating Flavio Cobolli 7-6, 6-3.

Medvedev will look to strengthen his position further when he plays Carlos Alcaraz on Wednesday afternoon. With victory against Cobolli, Medvedev extended an extraordinary record: the Russian has now won 42 of 43 matches this year when he has won the opening set.

Nakashima, the world number 19, defeated Daniil Medvedev at the Cincinnati Open final back in August. Which player do you think will win the 2026 ATP Finals? Nakashima lost the opening set 6-7, before roaring back to claim the next two sets 7-6, 6-1. It was Nakashima’s first triumph against Medvedev in four attempts.

items.title: Fils turns it around against Jodar to stay alive at the ATP Finals
paras: Arthur Fils beat Rafael Jodar 4-6, 6-2, 6-2 in 1h51 on Tuesday at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Frustrated after losing the first set, the Frenchman broke early in the second, mixed up his game and levelled their 2026 head-to-head at 2-2 before a decisive meeting with Alexander Zverev on Thursday.

After his opening defeat to Ben Shelton , the Frenchman stays in the race for the semi-finals in the John McEnroe Group, and gets his revenge after two defeats to the Spaniard this summer , in Washington and Montreal. At 1-1, he earned two break points on Jodar’s serve, then a third at 4-4, in a long game with several deuces. Serving at 4-5, Fils fell behind 15-40, saved a first set point, but not the second, and lost the set in 47 minutes.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
